THE RELEASE CONTRACT

Make the guardrails
visible.

Try the preflight with sample repository conditions. Versions compare numerically, not alphabetically. First release: 0.1.0; while major is zero, breaking changes raise minor.

This page does not inspect your repository. It previews tools/release.sh behavior; no tag or push is made.

SAME SOURCE, DIFFERENT EVENTS
Publish only
what the event means.
Each module workflow calls build-module.yml. Pull requests only build; main pushes publish changed modules; release tags build all four.
Repository namespace: ghcr.io/avarcorg. Images are public; hosts can pull without a registry login. POM versions tag local builds, not the published release names.
Main-push notification is best effort, after successful publish, same repository only. PRs, forks and releases do not notify. A deployment-side listener treats a message only as a hint and checks the registry. Automatic host deployment is not defined here.
CLEAN HISTORY, KEEP RELEASES
Retention is a rule.
Not a blanket delete.
Inspect a single synthetic image version. Weekly/on-demand cleanup protects release tags, snapshot, latest, and the newest five versions.
Policy-only preview; no registry is contacted. The actual workflow uses packages:write and supports dry run and retention inputs. Hosts select snapshot or release tags, never bare sha tags.
Notes live with the tag.
Each annotated tag message lists commit subjects since the previous release, one per line, including source work-item references. No separate changelog. If a signing key is configured, git tag -s signs it; otherwise it is annotated only.
Runs are not releases.
Workflow-run cleanup is separate: finished runs older than 30 days, preserving the newest five of each workflow. Queued and running runs stay. Permission: actions:write. Images, git tags and releases are unaffected.
Builds have boundaries.
Java/Node versions in the reusable workflow must match the POMs. Maven/wrapper/npm downloads are cached; pulled Docker images and pack-internal downloads are not. Stage uses snapshot; production uses release tags only when it exists.
All versions, conditions and command outputs above are specimens. This page does not create releases, publish images, remove packages, contact webhooks or deploy services.
